newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Sega and Bandai announce merger.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Sega and Bandai announce merger.

text.p: Sega Enterprises Ltd and Bandai Co Ltd said on Thursday they will merge on October 1, creating a formidable new world force in the toy and videogame market.

Bandai, a leading Japanese toy producer, is best known for its Power Ranger series of toys and has recently scored a hit with a "virtual pet" that it says is a sellout success. Sega is a leading producer of video games for both the home and arcade market but has been facing problems recently due to stiff competition.
While the companies called the deal a merger, they said that Bandai would be "dissolved" into the new company, which they said will be an unrivalled media entertainment firm.

For Sega, the deal offers a new product line when it is facing problems in its core business. Its Sega Saturn faces an increasingly difficult battle in the key U.S. market and it has been forced to cut its profit forecast for the fiscal year ending March 31.

Bandai has also had some problems from a slowing market. Its profits for the six months ending September 30 were down more than 50 percent and a spokesman said at the time that the company had misread market trends showing increased demand for low-priced toys.
